title: Dimension bound for an irreducible open complement
statement: Let $X$ be an irreducible topological space, $d\in\mathbb N$ and $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If $U$ is a nonempty open subset, then its complement is empty, or there exists $e\in\mathbb N$ with $e<d$ and $\dim(X\setminus U)\leq e$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. This requires neither Noetherianity nor separation.

proof.text: Every chain of irreducible closed subsets of Z=X minus U maps strictly increasingly to a chain in X. Since Z is closed these images remain closed; append the whole irreducible space X, which strictly contains every image because U is nonempty. Thus a chain in Z of length n implies n+1<=d.
If d=0, the closure of any point of Z would be a length-zero chain, contradicting 1<=0, so Z is empty. If d=e+1, every chain of Z has length at most e, so its Krull dimension is at most e and e<d.
